text: In 1912 Alfred Wegener proposed that the continents drift. Most geologists rejected it, partly because he had no mechanism; he died on the Greenland ice sheet in 1930, decades before plate tectonics proved him right.
In 1952 Marie Tharp spotted a rift valley running down the middle of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, evidence for continental drift. Her colleague Bruce Heezen at first dismissed it as "girl talk."
The summit of Mount Everest is marine limestone, laid down roughly 450 million years ago on a warm seafloor. It holds fragments of trilobites and crinoids.
California will not fall into the sea. Along the San Andreas Fault the Pacific Plate slides northwest past North America by a few centimeters a year, carrying Los Angeles slowly toward San Francisco.
Geologists still disagree about when plate tectonics began on Earth. Published estimates range from more than 4 billion years ago to less than 1 billion.
The Mohs scale (1812) only ranks which mineral scratches which. Measured with a sclerometer, diamond (10) is nearly four times as hard as corundum (9), which is only twice as hard as topaz (8).
About 300 m down in Mexico's Naica mine, a cave holds gypsum crystals more than 11 m long. The air reached 58 °C with 90 to 99% humidity; the cave was allowed to flood again in 2015.
Diamonds almost never come from coal. Most formed 150 km or more down in the mantle, and many are over a billion years old, older than the land plants whose remains make coal.
More than two-thirds of known mineral species probably exist only because of life, most of them thanks to the oxygen that photosynthesis added to the air and oceans.

Tambora's 1815 eruption in Indonesia, the largest in recorded history, helped bring the cold "Year Without a Summer" of 1816. Kept indoors by rain at Lake Geneva that June, Mary Shelley began Frankenstein.
The 1883 eruption of Krakatoa was heard about 4,800 km away on the island of Rodrigues, near Mauritius, and barographs worldwide recorded its pressure wave circling the globe more than three times.

Yellowstone is not "overdue." Its three great eruptions, about 2.08, 1.30 and 0.63 million years ago, are too few to set a schedule, and USGS scientists say the intervals are neither regular nor predictable.
In parts of the Grand Canyon, the Great Unconformity is a single surface where 1.2 to 1.6 billion years of rock record is missing. Why so much vanished, worldwide, is still debated.

In March 2024 geologists rejected a proposal to declare the Anthropocene a formal epoch starting in the 1950s, which would have been marked by plutonium from bomb tests in the mud of Crawford Lake, Ontario.
"We find no vestige of a beginning, no prospect of an end." (James Hutton, Theory of the Earth, 1788)
"The mind seemed to grow giddy by looking so far into the abyss of time." (John Playfair, Biographical Account of the Late Dr James Hutton, 1805)
Tyrannosaurus rex, which lived about 68 to 66 million years ago, is closer in time to us than to Stegosaurus, which died out roughly 145 million years ago or earlier.
In the late 1860s Edward Drinker Cope reconstructed the marine reptile Elasmosaurus with its head on the end of its tail. The blunder fed his bitter "Bone Wars" rivalry with Othniel Marsh.
Brontosaurus was sunk in 1903 as a mere synonym of Apatosaurus. In 2015 a large analysis of sauropod skeletons concluded it was distinct after all, and the name came back.
Rivers hold only about 0.006% of Earth's fresh water. Nearly 70% is frozen in ice and snow, and about 30% is groundwater.
All the gold ever mined, nearly 223,000 tonnes by mid-2026 according to the World Gold Council, would fit in a cube about 22.6 meters on a side.
When the Washington Monument was finished in 1884, its tip was a 2.8 kg pyramid of aluminum, then as costly as silver. Within two years the Hall-Héroult process made aluminum cheap.

Tiny zircon crystals from the Jack Hills of Western Australia are about 4.4 billion years old, the oldest known pieces of Earth, and hint at liquid water only about 150 million years after the planet formed.

About 1.7 billion years ago, uranium ore at Oklo in Gabon ran natural nuclear chain reactions on and off for hundreds of thousands of years. It was found in 1972, when its uranium came up short of uranium-235.
Radiocarbon cannot date dinosaurs. Carbon-14 has a half-life of about 5,730 years, so after roughly 50,000 years too little remains to measure; dinosaur ages come from isotopes such as uranium-lead.
In 1956 Clair Patterson dated Earth to about 4.55 billion years using lead from the Canyon Diablo meteorite. Fighting lead contamination in his lab led him to campaign against leaded gasoline.

In August 1996 NASA scientists announced possible fossil microbes in the Martian meteorite ALH84001, and President Clinton spoke about it on television. Most researchers now explain the features without life.

Saturn's moon Enceladus sprays plumes of salty water from an ocean beneath its ice. Phosphates were found in the spray in 2023; of the six key elements of life, only sulfur is not yet firmly detected.

Four billion years ago the Sun shone at only about 70% of its present brightness, too little to keep a modern Earth unfrozen, yet rocks show liquid water. Carl Sagan and George Mullen raised this paradox in 1972.
Pele's hair is volcanic glass spun into hair-thin threads when wind stretches droplets of fountaining lava. It is named after Pele, the Hawaiian deity of volcanoes.
